detail.body:
## Summary

Adds opt-in **HOST staging for NIXL prefill → decode transfers**: gather GPU rows into pinned host slots, transfer them into decode's pinned ring, then scatter into decode GPU memory. The existing NIXL planner still supplies the KV/state layouts and transfer rows.

```bash
# Set the same pinned-memory budget (MiB per worker) on prefill and decode.
export SGLANG_NIXL_HOST_STAGING_MB=1024
```

Unset or `0` disables HOST staging. The transfer backend is NIXL; auxiliary metadata continues through the existing NIXL path.

## Original and new SGL flow

### Stock NIXL / UCX — without GPUDirect RDMA

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant PG as Prefill GPU
    participant U as UCX host bounce buffers
    participant DG as Decode GPU
    loop Each UCX fragment of each WRITE
        PG->>U: Copy rows to host
        U->>DG: RDMA, then copy into the destination rows
    end
    PG-->>DG: KV_STATUS Success once every WRITE has settled
    Note over DG: Decode admits the request
```

### HOST staging — beneath the same planner

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant PG as Prefill GPU
    participant PS as Prefill pinned slots
    participant DR as Decode pinned ring
    participant DG as Decode GPU
    loop Each slot-sized part of each WRITE
        PG->>PS: Gather rows after the forward
        PS-->>DR: Request ring space
        DR-->>PS: Grant a region
        PS->>DR: One NIXL host-to-host WRITE
        DR->>DG: Validate rows, scatter, free the region
    end
    PG-->>DG: KV_STATUS Success once every ring WRITE has landed
    Note over DG: Decode admits once every granted region is scattered
```

Solid arrows: data. Dashed arrows: control. Gather and ring allocation can overlap; regions are freed after their scatter completes.

## Performance

### Latest · pure-upstream A/B · 2026-10-29

| Setup | Value |
|---|---|
| Build | Stock: upstream nightly `c10e0e17`; HOST: same image + PR files at `07e61a0555`. No downstream patches. |
| Hardware / model | B300, RoCE · Qwen3-8B · TP1 · 1 prefill + 1 decode |
| Requests per arm | Concurrency 1 · 32 × 29k and 16 × 64k cold prompts · 8 output tokens |
| KV payload / outcome | ≈4.0 / 8.8 GiB per request · all requests cold · zero request errors |

| Run | Handoff p50, 29k | Handoff p50, 64k | KV rate at 29k | TTFT p50, 29k / 64k |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| **HOST staging — this PR** | **250 ms** | **265 ms** | **16 GiB/s** | **783 / 1,927 ms** |
| Stock NIXL, GPUDirect RDMA off | 8,610 ms | 17,712 ms | 0.5 GiB/s | 9,095 / 19,237 ms |
| Stock NIXL, GPUDirect RDMA on | 47 ms | 51 ms | 86 GiB/s | 530 / 1,575 ms |

*Handoff* = `prefill_transfer_kv_cache`: end of the last chunk's forward → prefill observes transfer completion, for the slowest rank. At 64k, transfer overlaps earlier prefill work, so this is not the full transfer duration. *TTFT* = time to first token. Rates are in binary GiB/s.

### GLM-5.3 · GB300 · 2026-10-07

Earlier build; these measurements predate the latest upstream rebase.

GLM-5.3 NVFP4, GB300 1P1D, TP4/aDP4/EP4 per role, `UCX_IB_GPU_DIRECT_RDMA=n`. 32 unique cold prompts at 29k (single chunk), 16 at 64k (two chunks), concurrency 1. Handoff and TTFT are p50.

| Path | Optimistic prefill | Handoff, 29k | TTFT, 29k | Handoff, 64k | TTFT, 64k |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Stock | Off | 926.0 ms | 3.22 s | 1,414.5 ms | 6.52 s |
| HOST | Off | 15.9 ms | 2.31 s | 26.5 ms | 5.23 s |
| Stock | On | 926.0 ms | 3.20 s | 1,410.9 ms | 6.52 s |
| HOST | On | 16.3 ms | 2.30 s | 26.7 ms | 5.14 s |

## Correctness and failure handling

| Mechanism | Behavior |
|---|---|
| **Source lifetime** | Holds KV pages and metadata while asynchronous gathers or outstanding WRITEs can still read them, including failed requests across ranks. |
| **Decode completion** | Waits for prefill's Success and every granted ring region's scatter before admission. |
| **Destination validation** | Checks rows against registered memory and request-owned destinations before scatter. |
| **Large / strided transfers** | Splits oversized rows across slots; adapts HOST descriptors to the strided NIXL API without changing native descriptors. |
| **Cancellation** | Existing ABORT → drain → ABORT_ACK protocol gates release. |
| **Transport errors** | Settled errors fail the request; a WRITE unresolved past its deadline fail-stops its worker. Disconnected ring WRITEs fail their request; abandoned rooms notify decode promptly. |
| **Control backpressure** | Drain ACKs run off the progress thread; staging requests use nonblocking sends and lock acquisition. |
| **HiCache restore failure** | Fences prefill and waits for local restore DMA before freeing memory. |
| **Peer mismatch** | Refuses incompatible HOST configurations without crashing the worker. |

## Validation

### Earlier live stress · additional checks

| Check | GLM-5.3 | Kimi-K3 |
|---|---|---|
| Recall, 1k–108k tokens | 10/10 | 10/10 |
| Mixed 1k–120k load, 20–30% mid-stream cancels | ~11k requests, 0 KV-checksum mismatches | 354/354 at concurrency 32 |
| 150k–250k-token prompts | 58/58 | — |
| Cancel storm → recovery | 2,000 cancels → 534/534 | 715 cancels → 97/97 |
| Forced prefill kill | Decode stays up | Decode stays up |
| Forced decode kill | Prefill stays up | Prefill stays up |

inline_comments.body: Can we retain and retry the latest watermark on `zmq.Again`? The “next free” isn’t guaranteed: after wraparound, both prefill slots can be waiting on the final freeing scatter’s update. Drop that update and neither WRITE can post, so nothing else can scatter/free; the room hits the 15s post deadline. A regression test that drops that last update would catch this.

+"""NIXL WRITEs through pinned host memory, beneath native NIXL's transfer planner.
+
+The planners in nixl/conn.py reduce every KV and state transfer to (addr, len,
+device) rows and post them through NixlKVManager's transport seam. HOST staging
+replaces that seam: prefill packs a WRITE's source rows into a pinned slot behind a
+header and the WRITE's destination row table, then WRITEs the slot into the
+decode's pinned ring. Decode copies the header and table out of the ring, checks
+every row against the room's own registered memory and scatters the rows. Prefill
+reports Success only after every ring WRITE landed, and decode holds that Success
+back until every region it granted the room has been scattered, so native
+completion tracking is unchanged. Aux stays a native DRAM WRITE. No recovery of
+uncertain remote writes: a posted WRITE that cannot be settled fail-stops the
+process.
+"""

+import threading
+import time
+import traceback
+from collections import defaultdict, deque
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+
+import numpy as np
+import torch
+import zmq

+from sglang.srt.disaggregation.common.staging_buffer import (
+    StagingAllocator,
+    StagingBuffer,
+)

+from sglang.srt.environ import envs

+    from nixl._bindings import nixlNotFoundError, nixlRemoteDisconnectError
+except ImportError:  # NIXL-less CPU environments: no NIXL call raises these.
+
+    class nixlNotFoundError(RuntimeError):
+        pass
+
+    class nixlRemoteDisconnectError(RuntimeError):
+        pass

+SLOT_COUNT = 2
+VERSION = 4
+MAGIC = 0x33545348  # b"HST3"
+HEADER = np.dtype(
+    [
+        ("magic", "<u4"),
+        ("part", "<u4"),
+        ("parts", "<u4"),
+        ("reserved", "<u4"),
+        ("room", "<u8"),
+        ("seq", "<u8"),
+        ("group", "<u8"),
+        ("rows", "<u8"),
+        ("payload", "<u8"),
+    ]
+)
+ROW = np.dtype([("addr", "<u8"), ("len", "<u8")])
+PAYLOAD_ALIGN = 256
+# From STAGING_REQ, which precedes the grant: inside the decode's default 30 s
+# drain-ack wait, so an unacked room's ring regions are free to reuse on release.
+POST_DEADLINE_S, WRITE_DEADLINE_S = 15.0, 10.0
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+
+def check_release_timeout(timeout: float) -> None:
+    """Decode frees an unacked failed room's memory after this timeout; every
+    HOST writer WRITE (staged or native aux) settles or fail-stops within the
+    writer deadlines, so the timeout must outlast them."""
+    if timeout < POST_DEADLINE_S + WRITE_DEADLINE_S:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_DEFERRED_DECODE_KV_RELEASE_TIMEOUT={timeout} "
+            f"must be >= the HOST writer deadlines "
+            f"({POST_DEADLINE_S + WRITE_DEADLINE_S}s)"
+        )
+
+
+def payload_offset(n_rows: int) -> int:
+    end = HEADER.itemsize + n_rows * ROW.itemsize
+    return -(-end // PAYLOAD_ALIGN) * PAYLOAD_ALIGN
+
+
+def as_rows(rows):
+    """(addr, len) columns of planner rows; the device column is implied."""
+    rows = np.asarray(rows, dtype=np.uint64).reshape(-1, 3)
+    return rows[:, 0].copy(), rows[:, 1].copy()
+
+
+def coalesce(src, dst, lens):
+    """Merge rows that continue their predecessor on both sides."""
+    if len(lens) < 2:
+        return src, dst, lens
+    joins = (src[1:] == src[:-1] + lens[:-1]) & (dst[1:] == dst[:-1] + lens[:-1])
+    starts = np.flatnonzero(np.r_[True, ~joins])
+    return src[starts], dst[starts], np.add.reduceat(lens, starts)
+
+
+def copy_rows(dst, src, sizes, device, waits=()):
+    """Copy sizes[i] bytes src[i] -> dst[i] on the current stream after `waits`."""
+    from sglang.kernels.ops.kvcache.pd_dcp_gather import copy_byte_ranges
+
+    # Pinned and async: a pageable upload would block this thread until the
+    # stream's queued work (earlier scatters, producer waits) finished.
+    table = (
+        torch.from_numpy(np.stack([dst, src, sizes]).astype(np.int64))
+        .pin_memory()
+        .to(device, non_blocking=True)
+    )
+    stream = torch.cuda.current_stream(device)
+    for event in waits:
+        if event is not None:
+            stream.wait_event(event)
+    copy_byte_ranges(table, int(sizes.max()))
+

+@dataclass
+class HostWrite:
+    """Pseudo xfer handle the native transfer worker polls."""
+
+    parts: int
+    state: str = "PROC"  # PROC -> DONE | ERR
+    settled: int = 0
+    failed: bool = False
+
+    def settle(self, state="DONE"):
+        self.settled += 1
+        self.failed |= state == "ERR"
+        # Native treats ERR as settled and acks the room's drain, so report
+        # only once no part of this WRITE can still land in the peer's ring.
+        if self.settled == self.parts:
+            self.state = "ERR" if self.failed else "DONE"
+
+
+@dataclass
+class HostPart:
+    write: HostWrite
+    peer: str
+    room: int
+    seq: int
+    group: int
+    part: int
+    parts: int
+    src: np.ndarray
+    dst: np.ndarray
+    lens: np.ndarray
+    requested: float = 0.0
+
+    @property
+    def size(self) -> int:
+        return payload_offset(len(self.lens)) + int(self.lens.sum())
+
+
+@dataclass
+class HostDlist:
+    rows: np.ndarray
+    mem_kind: str
+
+
+@dataclass
+class HostSlot:
+    buffer: StagingBuffer
+    stream: object
+    part: HostPart | None = None
+    copy_done: object = None
+    handle: object = None
+    request: tuple | None = None  # Unsent STAGING_REQ: (endpoint, is_ipv6, parts).

+class HostStaging:
+    def __init__(self, manager):
+        self.manager = manager
+        args = manager.kv_args
+        # Capacity is the TOTAL pinned budget, not a per-slot multiplier.
+        self.capacity = manager.host_staging_bytes
+        self.slot_bytes = self.capacity // SLOT_COUNT
+        if self.slot_bytes < payload_offset(1) + PAYLOAD_ALIGN:
+            raise ValueError("Host staging capacity is too small")
+        if set(args.kv_data_mem_kinds) - {"VRAM"}:
+            raise ValueError("Host staging requires CUDA KV pools")
+        # FP4 pools keep scales outside the exported KV buffers, so no NIXL path
+        # (native included) moves them yet: refuse rather than send bare data.
+        if args.kv_cache_dtype_str == "nvfp4":
+            raise ValueError("NIXL PD does not transfer FP4 KV scales yet")
+        self.lock = threading.Lock()
+        # The transfer worker names the room whose batch it is posting.
+        self.batch = threading.local()
+        self.device = torch.device(f"cuda:{args.gpu_id}")
+        self.config = {
+            "version": VERSION,
+            "capacity": self.capacity,
+            "post_deadline_sec": POST_DEADLINE_S,
+            "write_deadline_sec": WRITE_DEADLINE_S,
+        }
+        self.slots, self.allocator = [], None
+        # Prefill: queued parts FIFO, per-room seqs and producer events.
+        self.queue = deque()
+        self.seqs = defaultdict(int)
+        self.ready = {}
+        self.failed_rooms = set()
+        if manager.disaggregation_mode == DisaggregationMode.PREFILL:
+            for _ in range(SLOT_COUNT):
+                buffer = StagingBuffer(
+                    self.slot_bytes, "cpu", args.gpu_id, pin_memory=True
+                )
+                manager._register_staging_memory(buffer.get_ptr(), self.slot_bytes)
+                self.slots.append(HostSlot(buffer, torch.cuda.Stream(self.device)))
+            threading.Thread(target=self.run, args=(self.worker,), daemon=True).start()
+        else:
+            check_release_timeout(
+                envs.SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_DEFERRED_DECODE_KV_RELEASE_TIMEOUT.get()
+            )
+            # One stream serializes the scatters; distinct ring regions are written
+            # concurrently and retired only by their own scatter events.
+            self.stream = torch.cuda.Stream(device=self.device)
+            self.allocator = StagingAllocator(
+                self.capacity, "cpu", args.gpu_id, pin_memory=True
+            )
+            manager._register_staging_memory(
+                self.allocator.get_base_ptr(), self.capacity
+            )
+
+    def config_mismatch(self, peer) -> bool:
+        return (
+            peer.host_staging_config != self.config
+            or peer.staging_base_ptr <= 0
+            or peer.staging_total_size != self.capacity
+        )
+
+    def run(self, operation, *args):
+        try:
+            return operation(*args)
+        except Exception as exc:
+            # Fail-stop is the contract for every HOST transport error, but keep
+            # the cause: a local bug must not read like an unfenced RDMA fault.
+            fail_stop(f"{operation.__name__}: {exc!r}\n{traceback.format_exc()}")
+
+    # -- Seam: NixlKVManager binds these over its native transport methods. ---
+
+    def prep_dlist(self, peer_name, stride_descs, mem_kind):
+        # Planners hand packed Nx5 stride runs; the host path needs one flat
+        # (addr, len, device) row per block.
+        # Keeps every prepared row in host RAM (slots x layers x 24 B per
+        # peer); store per-entry (base, stride, count) if that ever matters.
+        rows = self.manager._expand_stride_descs(stride_descs)
+        return HostDlist(np.asarray(rows, dtype=np.uint64).reshape(-1, 3), mem_kind)
+
+    def post_prepped(self, peer_name, src, src_indices, dst, dst_indices, what):
+        return self.post_write(
+            peer_name,
+            src.rows[src_indices],
+            src.mem_kind,
+            dst.rows[dst_indices],
+            dst.mem_kind,
+            what,
+        )
+
+    def post_write(
+        self, peer_name, src_rows, src_mem_kind, dst_rows, dst_mem_kind, what
+    ):
+        manager = self.manager
+        if src_mem_kind == dst_mem_kind == "DRAM":
+            # Aux: registered host memory on both sides, a native WRITE.
+            return type(manager)._post_write(
+                manager,
+                peer_name,
+                src_rows,
+                src_mem_kind,
+                dst_rows,
+                dst_mem_kind,
+                what,
+            )
+        if src_mem_kind != "VRAM" or dst_mem_kind != "VRAM":
+            raise NotImplementedError(
+                f"Host staging does not stage {src_mem_kind}->{dst_mem_kind} {what}"
+            )
+        room = self.batch.room
+        src, src_lens = as_rows(src_rows)
+        dst, dst_lens = as_rows(dst_rows)
+        if not np.array_equal(src_lens, dst_lens):
+            raise ValueError(f"Host staging {what} row lengths differ")
+        # Zero-length rows are placeholder entries (e.g. DSA skip-topk layers).
+        live = src_lens > 0
+        src, dst, lens = coalesce(src[live], dst[live], src_lens[live])
+        if not len(lens):
+            return HostWrite(1, "DONE")  # No bytes: nothing to stage.
+        budget = self.slot_bytes - payload_offset(0) - PAYLOAD_ALIGN
+        # Split rows (coalesced or native) larger than a slot: validation and the
+        # byte copy take any sub-range of a row.
+        cap = budget - ROW.itemsize  # > 0: __init__ keeps budget >= PAYLOAD_ALIGN.
+        if (lens > cap).any():
+            n = ((lens + (cap - 1)) // cap).astype(np.int64)
+            rep = np.repeat(np.arange(len(lens)), n)
+            piece = np.arange(n.sum()) - np.repeat(np.cumsum(n) - n, n)
+            off = piece.astype(np.uint64) * np.uint64(cap)
+            src, dst = src[rep] + off, dst[rep] + off
+            lens = np.minimum(lens[rep] - off, np.uint64(cap))
+        # Split on row boundaries so each part fits one slot.
+        cuts, used = [0], 0
+        for i, n in enumerate(lens.tolist()):
+            if used + n + ROW.itemsize > budget:
+                cuts.append(i)
+                used = 0
+            used += n + ROW.itemsize
+        cuts.append(len(lens))
+        write = HostWrite(len(cuts) - 1)
+        with self.lock:
+            if self._failed(room):
+                write.state = "DONE"  # Nothing posts for a failed room.
+                return write
+            seqs = self.seqs
+            group = seqs[room, peer_name]
+            seqs[room, peer_name] += write.parts
+            for part, (a, b) in enumerate(zip(cuts, cuts[1:])):
+                self.queue.append(
+                    HostPart(
+                        write,
+                        peer_name,
+                        room,
+                        group + part,
+                        group,
+                        part,
+                        write.parts,
+                        src[a:b],
+                        dst[a:b],
+                        lens[a:b],
+                    )
+                )
+        return write
+
+    def xfer_state(self, handle):
+        if isinstance(handle, HostWrite):
+            return handle.state
+        try:
+            return self.manager.agent.check_xfer_state(handle)
+        except nixlRemoteDisconnectError:
+            # NIXL raises failed states instead of returning "ERR". A disconnect
+            # means the endpoint failed, which completes every request it carries
+            # (a WRITE split across threads reports only after all of its chunks),
+            # so nothing lands later: settled.
+            return "ERR"
+
+    # -- Prefill pipeline -----------------------------------------------------
+
+    def _failed(self, room) -> bool:
+        # A cleared room is gone, not pending: treat it as failed.
+        return room in self.failed_rooms or self.manager.request_status.get(room) in (
+            None,
+            KVPoll.Failed,
+        )
+
+    def fail_room(self, room):
+        """Drop a failed room's unposted parts. Caller holds self.lock."""
+        self.failed_rooms.add(room)
+        for part in [p for p in self.queue if p.room == room]:
+            self.queue.remove(part)
+            part.write.settle()
+
+    def gathering(self, room) -> bool:
+        """Whether a part of room may still read its source pages."""
+        with self.lock:
+            return any(p.room == room for p in self.queue) or any(
+                s.part is not None
+                and s.part.room == room
+                and (s.copy_done is None or not s.copy_done.query())
+                for s in self.slots
+            )
+
+    def drain_gathers(self, room):
+        if not self.gathering(room):
+            return
+        started = time.monotonic()
+        logger.info("Draining host staging gathers for room=%s", room)
+        while self.gathering(room):
+            if time.monotonic() - started >= POST_DEADLINE_S + WRITE_DEADLINE_S:
+                fail_stop(f"Host staging gather drain timed out for room {room}")
+            time.sleep(0.0005)
+        logger.info(
+            "Drained host staging gathers for room=%s in %.3fs",
+            room,
+            time.monotonic() - started,
+        )
+
+    def forget_room(self, room):
+        with self.lock:
+            self.failed_rooms.discard(room)
+            self.ready.pop(room, None)
+            for key in [k for k in self.seqs if k[0] == room]:
+                del self.seqs[key]
+
+    def worker(self):
+        torch.cuda.set_device(self.device)
+        while True:
+            self.progress()
+            time.sleep(0.0005)
+
+    def progress(self):
+        self.manager._reap_abandoned()
+        for slot in self.slots:
+            if slot.part is not None:
+                self._advance(slot)
+        for slot in self.slots:
+            if slot.part is None:
+                with self.lock:
+                    if not self.queue:
+                        return
+                    part = self.queue.popleft()
+                    req = self.manager.transfer_infos.get(part.room, {}).get(part.peer)
+                    if req is None:  # Room cleared since; nothing to post.
+                        part.write.settle()
+                        continue
+                    # Claimed under the lock: gathering() never misses this part.
+                    slot.part, slot.handle, slot.copy_done = part, None, None
+                self._start(slot, part, req)
+
+    def _start(self, slot, part, req):
+        from sglang.srt.utils.network import NetworkAddress
+
+        manager = self.manager
+        part.requested = time.monotonic()
+        view = slot.buffer.buffer.numpy()
+        header = np.zeros(1, HEADER)
+        header[0] = (
+            MAGIC,
+            part.part,
+            part.parts,
+            0,
+            part.room,
+            part.seq,
+            part.group,
+            len(part.lens),
+            int(part.lens.sum()),
+        )
+        view[: HEADER.itemsize] = header.view(np.uint8)
+        table = np.empty(len(part.lens), ROW)
+        table["addr"], table["len"] = part.dst, part.lens
+        table_end = HEADER.itemsize + table.nbytes
+        view[HEADER.itemsize : table_end] = table.view(np.uint8)
+        copy_done = torch.cuda.Event()
+        with torch.cuda.stream(slot.stream):
+            start = slot.buffer.get_ptr() + payload_offset(len(part.lens))
+            offsets = np.r_[0, np.cumsum(part.lens)[:-1]].astype(np.uint64)
+            copy_rows(
+                offsets + np.uint64(start),
+                part.src,
+                part.lens,
+                self.device,
+                waits=self.ready.get(part.room, ()),
+            )
+            copy_done.record(slot.stream)
+        slot.copy_done = copy_done  # Published once recorded.
+        address = NetworkAddress(req.endpoint, req.dst_port)
+        slot.request = (
+            address.to_tcp(),
+            address.is_ipv6,
+            [
+                b"STAGING_REQ",
+                str(part.room).encode(),
+                str(part.seq).encode(),
+                str(part.size).encode(),
+                part.peer.encode(),
+                manager.agent.name.encode(),
+                # Our bootstrap endpoint: the response goes to this writer only.
+                str(manager.local_ip).encode(),
+                str(manager.rank_port).encode(),
+            ],
+        )
+        self._try_send(slot)
+
+    def _try_send(self, slot):
+        """Send the slot's STAGING_REQ if the socket takes it now; else retry.
+
+        Never block this thread: it alone enforces every slot's WRITE deadline,
+        which decode's ring reuse after its drain-ack wait relies on.
+        """
+        endpoint, is_ipv6, parts = slot.request
+        manager = self.manager
+        sock = manager._connect(endpoint, is_ipv6=is_ipv6)
+        lock = manager._socket_send_locks[endpoint]
+        if not lock.acquire(blocking=False):
+            return
+        try:
+            sock.send_multipart(parts, flags=zmq.NOBLOCK)
+            slot.request = None
+        except zmq.Again:
+            pass
+        finally:
+            lock.release()
+
+    def _advance(self, slot):
+        part, manager = slot.part, self.manager
+        if slot.handle is None:
+            if slot.request is not None:
+                self._try_send(slot)
+            # Nothing leaves the slot, not even a dropped part, while its gather
+            # (queued behind the forward) may still write it.
+            if not slot.copy_done.query():
+                return
+            with self.lock:
+                req = manager.transfer_infos.get(part.room, {}).get(part.peer)
+                if req is None or self._failed(part.room):
+                    # Unposted: the peer never sees this part.
+                    self._finish(slot, "DONE")
+                    return
+                if time.monotonic() - part.requested >= POST_DEADLINE_S:
+                    logger.error(
+                        "Host staging part timed out before posting room=%s seq=%s",
+                        part.room,
+                        part.seq,
+                    )
+                    self._finish(slot, "ERR")
+                    return
+                staging = req.staging
+                # Native set_chunk publishes ends last, after offsets/rounds.
+                if (
+                    staging is None
+                    or part.seq >= len(staging.ends)
+                    or staging.ends[part.seq] < 0
+                ):
+                    return
+                offset, rnd, end = (
+                    staging.offsets[part.seq],
+                    staging.rounds[part.seq],
+                    staging.ends[part.seq],
+                )
+                if offset < 0 or end != offset + part.size or end > self.capacity:
+                    raise ValueError("Invalid host staging allocation response")
+                if not manager._is_watermark_ready(part.peer, rnd, end):
+                    return
+                peer = manager.decode_kv_args_table[part.peer]
+                # Posted under the lock fail_room() takes: a failure either sees
+                # this part queued (dropped) or posted (fenced by the drain ack).
+                try:
+                    slot.handle = self._post_ring_write(
+                        slot, part, peer.staging_base_ptr + offset
+                    )
+                except Exception as exc:
+                    # Refused for a dropped peer (createXferReq raises), or
+                    # failed posting on a dead endpoint (_post_xfer wraps it).
+                    # A one-row WRITE rides a single endpoint and a failed post
+                    # releases what it began: nothing is running.
+                    cause = exc.__cause__ or exc
+                    if not isinstance(
+                        cause, (nixlNotFoundError, nixlRemoteDisconnectError)
+                    ):
+                        raise
+                    logger.warning(
+                        "Host staging WRITE not posted room=%s seq=%s: %r",
+                        part.room,
+                        part.seq,
+                        exc,
+                    )
+                    self._finish(slot, "ERR")
+            return
+        try:
+            state = self.xfer_state(slot.handle)
+        except nixlNotFoundError:
+            # A disconnect seen on another handle dropped this peer's metadata, so
+            # NIXL cannot read this WRITE until the transfer worker reloads it
+            # (conn.py fails a batch whose WRITE has a failed part, which runs
+            # that reload). It may still be writing: keep it under its deadline.
+            state = "PROC"
+        if state == "PROC":
+            if time.monotonic() - part.requested >= POST_DEADLINE_S + WRITE_DEADLINE_S:
+                fail_stop(f"Host staging WRITE timeout room={part.room} seq={part.seq}")
+            return
+        # ERR (e.g. the peer died) has settled: it lands nothing later, and the
+        # decode holds the region until the drain ack. Fail the room like native.
+        manager.agent.release_xfer_handle(slot.handle)
+        with self.lock:
+            self._finish(slot, "DONE" if state == "DONE" else "ERR")
+
+    def _post_ring_write(self, slot, part, dst_ptr):
+        # The ring WRITE carries its own NIXL notification: decode validates and
+        # scatters a part once NIXL reports it landed.
+        agent = self.manager.agent
+        handle = agent.initialize_xfer(
+            "WRITE",
+            agent.get_xfer_descs([(slot.buffer.get_ptr(), part.size, 0)], "DRAM"),
+            agent.get_xfer_descs([(dst_ptr, part.size, 0)], "DRAM"),
+            part.peer,
+            f"{part.room}_hst_{part.seq}".encode("ascii"),
+        )
+        return self.manager._start_xfer(handle, "host staging WRITE")
+
+    def _finish(self, slot, state):
+        # Caller holds self.lock.
+        slot.part.write.settle(state)
+        slot.part = slot.handle = slot.request = None

+class HostDecodeStagingHandler:
+    """Decode side of HOST staging: ring allocation, row validation and scatter.
+
+    Implements the decode staging-handler interface DecodeTransferQueue drives
+    (register/unregister, is_done/is_failed/advance_scatter). It moves bytes
+    only: rows arrive already planned, so it needs no KV layout.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self, manager, scheduler, tp_rank):
+        host = manager.host_staging

+        self.completion_timeout = float(
+            envs.SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_WAITING_TIMEOUT.get()
+        )
+        self._room_to_decode_req = {}
+        self._room_to_receiver = {}

+        # Registered destinations: (base, length, item bytes, owner), by base.
+        args = manager.kv_args
+        regions = [
+            (ptr, length, item, "kv")
+            for ptr, length, item in zip(
+                args.kv_data_ptrs, args.kv_data_lens, args.kv_item_lens
+            )

+            zip(args.state_data_ptrs, args.state_data_lens, args.state_item_lens)
+        ):
+            regions += [
+                (ptr, length, item, comp)
+                for ptr, length, item in zip(ptrs, lengths, items)
+            ]

+every row against the room's own registered memory and scatters the rows. Prefill

+back until every region it granted the room has been scattered, so native
+completion tracking is unchanged. Aux stays a native DRAM WRITE. No recovery of
+uncertain remote writes: a posted WRITE that cannot be settled fail-stops the

+import threading

+    class nixlNotFoundError(RuntimeError):
+        pass
+
+    class nixlRemoteDisconnectError(RuntimeError):
+        pass

+        ("part", "<u4"),
+        ("parts", "<u4"),
+        ("reserved", "<u4"),
+        ("room", "<u8"),
+        ("seq", "<u8"),
+        ("group", "<u8"),
+        ("rows", "<u8"),

+        pass
+
+    class nixlRemoteDisconnectError(RuntimeError):
+        pass
+
+
+SLOT_COUNT = 2
+VERSION = 4
+MAGIC = 0x33545348  # b"HST3"
+HEADER = np.dtype(
+    [
+        ("magic", "<u4"),
+        ("part", "<u4"),
+        ("parts", "<u4"),
+        ("reserved", "<u4"),
+        ("room", "<u8"),
+        ("seq", "<u8"),
+        ("group", "<u8"),
+        ("rows", "<u8"),
+        ("payload", "<u8"),
+    ]
+)
+ROW = np.dtype([("addr", "<u8"), ("len", "<u8")])
+PAYLOAD_ALIGN = 256
+# From STAGING_REQ, which precedes the grant: inside the decode's default 30 s
+# drain-ack wait, so an unacked room's ring regions are free to reuse on release.
+POST_DEADLINE_S, WRITE_DEADLINE_S = 15.0, 10.0
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+
+def check_release_timeout(timeout: float) -> None:
+    """Decode frees an unacked failed room's memory after this timeout; every
+    HOST writer WRITE (staged or native aux) settles or fail-stops within the
+    writer deadlines, so the timeout must outlast them."""
+    if timeout < POST_DEADLINE_S + WRITE_DEADLINE_S:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_DEFERRED_DECODE_KV_RELEASE_TIMEOUT={timeout} "
+            f"must be >= the HOST writer deadlines "
+            f"({POST_DEADLINE_S + WRITE_DEADLINE_S}s)"
+        )
+
+
+def payload_offset(n_rows: int) -> int:
+    end = HEADER.itemsize + n_rows * ROW.itemsize
+    return -(-end // PAYLOAD_ALIGN) * PAYLOAD_ALIGN
+
+
+def as_rows(rows):
+    """(addr, len) columns of planner rows; the device column is implied."""
+    rows = np.asarray(rows, dtype=np.uint64).reshape(-1, 3)
+    return rows[:, 0].copy(), rows[:, 1].copy()
+
+
+def coalesce(src, dst, lens):
+    """Merge rows that continue their predecessor on both sides."""
+    if len(lens) < 2:
+        return src, dst, lens
+    joins = (src[1:] == src[:-1] + lens[:-1]) & (dst[1:] == dst[:-1] + lens[:-1])
+    starts = np.flatnonzero(np.r_[True, ~joins])
+    return src[starts], dst[starts], np.add.reduceat(lens, starts)
+
+
+def copy_rows(dst, src, sizes, device, waits=()):
+    """Copy sizes[i] bytes src[i] -> dst[i] on the current stream after `waits`."""
+    from sglang.kernels.ops.kvcache.pd_dcp_gather import copy_byte_ranges
+
+    # Pinned and async: a pageable upload would block this thread until the
+    # stream's queued work (earlier scatters, producer waits) finished.
+    table = (
+        torch.from_numpy(np.stack([dst, src, sizes]).astype(np.int64))
+        .pin_memory()
+        .to(device, non_blocking=True)
+    )
+    stream = torch.cuda.current_stream(device)
+    for event in waits:
+        if event is not None:
+            stream.wait_event(event)
+    copy_byte_ranges(table, int(sizes.max()))
+
+
+@dataclass
+class HostWrite:
+    """Pseudo xfer handle the native transfer worker polls."""
+
+    parts: int
+    state: str = "PROC"  # PROC -> DONE | ERR
+    settled: int = 0
+    failed: bool = False
+
+    def settle(self, state="DONE"):
+        self.settled += 1
+        self.failed |= state == "ERR"
+        # Native treats ERR as settled and acks the room's drain, so report
+        # only once no part of this WRITE can still land in the peer's ring.
+        if self.settled == self.parts:
+            self.state = "ERR" if self.failed else "DONE"
+
+
+@dataclass
+class HostPart:
+    write: HostWrite
+    peer: str
+    room: int
+    seq: int
+    group: int
+    part: int
+    parts: int
+    src: np.ndarray
+    dst: np.ndarray
+    lens: np.ndarray
+    requested: float = 0.0
+
+    @property
+    def size(self) -> int:
+        return payload_offset(len(self.lens)) + int(self.lens.sum())
+
+
+@dataclass
+class HostDlist:
+    rows: np.ndarray
+    mem_kind: str
+
+
+@dataclass
+class HostSlot:
+    buffer: StagingBuffer
+    stream: object
+    part: HostPart | None = None
+    copy_done: object = None
+    handle: object = None
+    request: tuple | None = None  # Unsent STAGING_REQ: (endpoint, is_ipv6, parts).
+
+
+class HostStaging:
+    def __init__(self, manager):
+        self.manager = manager
+        args = manager.kv_args
+        # Capacity is the TOTAL pinned budget, not a per-slot multiplier.
+        self.capacity = manager.host_staging_bytes
+        self.slot_bytes = self.capacity // SLOT_COUNT
+        if self.slot_bytes < payload_offset(1) + PAYLOAD_ALIGN:
+            raise ValueError("Host staging capacity is too small")
+        if set(args.kv_data_mem_kinds) - {"VRAM"}:
+            raise ValueError("Host staging requires CUDA KV pools")
+        # FP4 pools keep scales outside the exported KV buffers, so no NIXL path
+        # (native included) moves them yet: refuse rather than send bare data.
+        if args.kv_cache_dtype_str == "nvfp4":
+            raise ValueError("NIXL PD does not transfer FP4 KV scales yet")
+        self.lock = threading.Lock()
+        # The transfer worker names the room whose batch it is posting.
+        self.batch = threading.local()
+        self.device = torch.device(f"cuda:{args.gpu_id}")
+        self.config = {
+            "version": VERSION,
+            "capacity": self.capacity,
+            "post_deadline_sec": POST_DEADLINE_S,
+            "write_deadline_sec": WRITE_DEADLINE_S,
+        }
+        self.slots, self.allocator = [], None
+        # Prefill: queued parts FIFO, per-room seqs and producer events.
+        self.queue = deque()
+        self.seqs = defaultdict(int)
+        self.ready = {}
+        self.failed_rooms = set()
+        if manager.disaggregation_mode == DisaggregationMode.PREFILL:
+            for _ in range(SLOT_COUNT):
+                buffer = StagingBuffer(
+                    self.slot_bytes, "cpu", args.gpu_id, pin_memory=True
+                )
+                manager._register_staging_memory(buffer.get_ptr(), self.slot_bytes)
+                self.slots.append(HostSlot(buffer, torch.cuda.Stream(self.device)))
+            threading.Thread(target=self.run, args=(self.worker,), daemon=True).start()
+        else:
+            check_release_timeout(
+                envs.SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_DEFERRED_DECODE_KV_RELEASE_TIMEOUT.get()
+            )
+            # One stream serializes the scatters; distinct ring regions are written
+            # concurrently and retired only by their own scatter events.
+            self.stream = torch.cuda.Stream(device=self.device)
+            self.allocator = StagingAllocator(
+                self.capacity, "cpu", args.gpu_id, pin_memory=True
+            )
+            manager._register_staging_memory(
+                self.allocator.get_base_ptr(), self.capacity
+            )
+
+    def config_mismatch(self, peer) -> bool:
+        return (
+            peer.host_staging_config != self.config
+            or peer.staging_base_ptr <= 0
+            or peer.staging_total_size != self.capacity
+        )
+
+    def run(self, operation, *args):
+        try:
+            return operation(*args)
+        except Exception as exc:
+            # Fail-stop is the contract for every HOST transport error, but keep
+            # the cause: a local bug must not read like an unfenced RDMA fault.
+            fail_stop(f"{operation.__name__}: {exc!r}\n{traceback.format_exc()}")
+
+    # -- Seam: NixlKVManager binds these over its native transport methods. ---
+
+    def prep_dlist(self, peer_name, stride_descs, mem_kind):
+        # Planners hand packed Nx5 stride runs; the host path needs one flat
+        # (addr, len, device) row per block.
+        # Keeps every prepared row in host RAM (slots x layers x 24 B per
+        # peer); store per-entry (base, stride, count) if that ever matters.
+        rows = self.manager._expand_stride_descs(stride_descs)
+        return HostDlist(np.asarray(rows, dtype=np.uint64).reshape(-1, 3), mem_kind)
+
+    def post_prepped(self, peer_name, src, src_indices, dst, dst_indices, what):
+        return self.post_write(
+            peer_name,
+            src.rows[src_indices],
+            src.mem_kind,
+            dst.rows[dst_indices],
+            dst.mem_kind,
+            what,
+        )
+
+    def post_write(
+        self, peer_name, src_rows, src_mem_kind, dst_rows, dst_mem_kind, what
+    ):
+        manager = self.manager
+        if src_mem_kind == dst_mem_kind == "DRAM":
+            # Aux: registered host memory on both sides, a native WRITE.
+            return type(manager)._post_write(
+                manager,
+                peer_name,
+                src_rows,
+                src_mem_kind,
+                dst_rows,
+                dst_mem_kind,
+                what,
+            )
+        if src_mem_kind != "VRAM" or dst_mem_kind != "VRAM":
+            raise NotImplementedError(
+                f"Host staging does not stage {src_mem_kind}->{dst_mem_kind} {what}"
+            )
+        room = self.batch.room
+        src, src_lens = as_rows(src_rows)
+        dst, dst_lens = as_rows(dst_rows)
+        if not np.array_equal(src_lens, dst_lens):
+            raise ValueError(f"Host staging {what} row lengths differ")
+        # Zero-length rows are placeholder entries (e.g. DSA skip-topk layers).
+        live = src_lens > 0
+        src, dst, lens = coalesce(src[live], dst[live], src_lens[live])
+        if not len(lens):
+            return HostWrite(1, "DONE")  # No bytes: nothing to stage.
+        budget = self.slot_bytes - payload_offset(0) - PAYLOAD_ALIGN
+        # Split rows (coalesced or native) larger than a slot: validation and the
+        # byte copy take any sub-range of a row.
+        cap = budget - ROW.itemsize  # > 0: __init__ keeps budget >= PAYLOAD_ALIGN.
+        if (lens > cap).any():
+            n = ((lens + (cap - 1)) // cap).astype(np.int64)
+            rep = np.repeat(np.arange(len(lens)), n)
+            piece = np.arange(n.sum()) - np.repeat(np.cumsum(n) - n, n)
+            off = piece.astype(np.uint64) * np.uint64(cap)
+            src, dst = src[rep] + off, dst[rep] + off
+            lens = np.minimum(lens[rep] - off, np.uint64(cap))
+        # Split on row boundaries so each part fits one slot.
+        cuts, used = [0], 0
+        for i, n in enumerate(lens.tolist()):
+            if used + n + ROW.itemsize > budget:
+                cuts.append(i)
+                used = 0
+            used += n + ROW.itemsize
+        cuts.append(len(lens))
+        write = HostWrite(len(cuts) - 1)
+        with self.lock:
+            if self._failed(room):
+                write.state = "DONE"  # Nothing posts for a failed room.
+                return write
+            seqs = self.seqs
+            group = seqs[room, peer_name]
+            seqs[room, peer_name] += write.parts
+            for part, (a, b) in enumerate(zip(cuts, cuts[1:])):
+                self.queue.append(
+                    HostPart(
+                        write,
+                        peer_name,
+                        room,
+                        group + part,
+                        group,
+                        part,
+                        write.parts,
+                        src[a:b],
+                        dst[a:b],
+                        lens[a:b],
+                    )
+                )
+        return write
+
+    def xfer_state(self, handle):
+        if isinstance(handle, HostWrite):
+            return handle.state
+        try:
+            return self.manager.agent.check_xfer_state(handle)
+        except nixlRemoteDisconnectError:
+            # NIXL raises failed states instead of returning "ERR". A disconnect
+            # means the endpoint failed, which completes every request it carries
+            # (a WRITE split across threads reports only after all of its chunks),
+            # so nothing lands later: settled.
+            return "ERR"
+
+    # -- Prefill pipeline -----------------------------------------------------
+
+    def _failed(self, room) -> bool:
+        # A cleared room is gone, not pending: treat it as failed.
+        return room in self.failed_rooms or self.manager.request_status.get(room) in (
+            None,
+            KVPoll.Failed,
+        )
+
+    def fail_room(self, room):
+        """Drop a failed room's unposted parts. Caller holds self.lock."""
+        self.failed_rooms.add(room)
+        for part in [p for p in self.queue if p.room == room]:
+            self.queue.remove(part)
+            part.write.settle()
+
+    def gathering(self, room) -> bool:
+        """Whether a part of room may still read its source pages."""
+        with self.lock:
+            return any(p.room == room for p in self.queue) or any(
+                s.part is not None
+                and s.part.room == room
+                and (s.copy_done is None or not s.copy_done.query())
+                for s in self.slots
+            )
+
+    def drain_gathers(self, room):
+        if not self.gathering(room):
+            return
+        started = time.monotonic()
+        logger.info("Draining host staging gathers for room=%s", room)
+        while self.gathering(room):
+            if time.monotonic() - started >= POST_DEADLINE_S + WRITE_DEADLINE_S:
+                fail_stop(f"Host staging gather drain timed out for room {room}")
+            time.sleep(0.0005)
+        logger.info(
+            "Drained host staging gathers for room=%s in %.3fs",
+            room,
+            time.monotonic() - started,
+        )
+
+    def forget_room(self, room):
+        with self.lock:
+            self.failed_rooms.discard(room)
+            self.ready.pop(room, None)
+            for key in [k for k in self.seqs if k[0] == room]:
+                del self.seqs[key]
+
+    def worker(self):
+        torch.cuda.set_device(self.device)
+        while True:
+            self.progress()
+            time.sleep(0.0005)
+
+    def progress(self):
+        self.manager._reap_abandoned()
+        for slot in self.slots:
+            if slot.part is not None:
+                self._advance(slot)
+        for slot in self.slots:
+            if slot.part is None:
+                with self.lock:
+                    if not self.queue:
+                        return
+                    part = self.queue.popleft()
+                    req = self.manager.transfer_infos.get(part.room, {}).get(part.peer)
+                    if req is None:  # Room cleared since; nothing to post.
+                        part.write.settle()
+                        continue
+                    # Claimed under the lock: gathering() never misses this part.
+                    slot.part, slot.handle, slot.copy_done = part, None, None
+                self._start(slot, part, req)
+
+    def _start(self, slot, part, req):
+        from sglang.srt.utils.network import NetworkAddress
+
+        manager = self.manager
+        part.requested = time.monotonic()
+        view = slot.buffer.buffer.numpy()
+        header = np.zeros(1, HEADER)
+        header[0] = (
+            MAGIC,
+            part.part,
+            part.parts,
+            0,
+            part.room,
+            part.seq,
+            part.group,
+            len(part.lens),
+            int(part.lens.sum()),
+        )
+        view[: HEADER.itemsize] = header.view(np.uint8)
+        table = np.empty(len(part.lens), ROW)
+        table["addr"], table["len"] = part.dst, part.lens
+        table_end = HEADER.itemsize + table.nbytes
+        view[HEADER.itemsize : table_end] = table.view(np.uint8)
+        copy_done = torch.cuda.Event()
+        with torch.cuda.stream(slot.stream):
+            start = slot.buffer.get_ptr() + payload_offset(len(part.lens))
+            offsets = np.r_[0, np.cumsum(part.lens)[:-1]].astype(np.uint64)
+            copy_rows(
+                offsets + np.uint64(start),
+                part.src,
+                part.lens,
+                self.device,
+                waits=self.ready.get(part.room, ()),
+            )
+            copy_done.record(slot.stream)
+        slot.copy_done = copy_done  # Published once recorded.
+        address = NetworkAddress(req.endpoint, req.dst_port)
+        slot.request = (
+            address.to_tcp(),
+            address.is_ipv6,
+            [
+                b"STAGING_REQ",
+                str(part.room).encode(),
+                str(part.seq).encode(),
+                str(part.size).encode(),
+                part.peer.encode(),
+                manager.agent.name.encode(),
+                # Our bootstrap endpoint: the response goes to this writer only.
+                str(manager.local_ip).encode(),
+                str(manager.rank_port).encode(),
+            ],
+        )
+        self._try_send(slot)
+
+    def _try_send(self, slot):
+        """Send the slot's STAGING_REQ if the socket takes it now; else retry.
+
+        Never block this thread: it alone enforces every slot's WRITE deadline,
+        which decode's ring reuse after its drain-ack wait relies on.
+        """
+        endpoint, is_ipv6, parts = slot.request
+        manager = self.manager
+        sock = manager._connect(endpoint, is_ipv6=is_ipv6)
+        lock = manager._socket_send_locks[endpoint]
+        if not lock.acquire(blocking=False):
+            return
+        try:
+            sock.send_multipart(parts, flags=zmq.NOBLOCK)
+            slot.request = None
+        except zmq.Again:
+            pass
+        finally:
+            lock.release()
+
+    def _advance(self, slot):
+        part, manager = slot.part, self.manager
+        if slot.handle is None:
+            if slot.request is not None:
+                self._try_send(slot)
+            # Nothing leaves the slot, not even a dropped part, while its gather
+            # (queued behind the forward) may still write it.
+            if not slot.copy_done.query():
+                return
+            with self.lock:
+                req = manager.transfer_infos.get(part.room, {}).get(part.peer)
+                if req is None or self._failed(part.room):
+                    # Unposted: the peer never sees this part.
+                    self._finish(slot, "DONE")
+                    return
+                if time.monotonic() - part.requested >= POST_DEADLINE_S:
+                    logger.error(
+                        "Host staging part timed out before posting room=%s seq=%s",
+                        part.room,
+                        part.seq,
+                    )
+                    self._finish(slot, "ERR")
+                    return
+                staging = req.staging
+                # Native set_chunk publishes ends last, after offsets/rounds.
+                if (
+                    staging is None
+                    or part.seq >= len(staging.ends)
+                    or staging.ends[part.seq] < 0
+                ):
+                    return
+                offset, rnd, end = (
+                    staging.offsets[part.seq],
+                    staging.rounds[part.seq],
+                    staging.ends[part.seq],
+                )
+                if offset < 0 or end != offset + part.size or end > self.capacity:
+                    raise ValueError("Invalid host staging allocation response")
+                if not manager._is_watermark_ready(part.peer, rnd, end):
+                    return
+                peer = manager.decode_kv_args_table[part.peer]
+                # Posted under the lock fail_room() takes: a failure either sees
+                # this part queued (dropped) or posted (fenced by the drain ack).
+                try:
+                    slot.handle = self._post_ring_write(
+                        slot, part, peer.staging_base_ptr + offset
+                    )
+                except Exception as exc:
+                    # Refused for a dropped peer (createXferReq raises), or
+                    # failed posting on a dead endpoint (_post_xfer wraps it).
+                    # A one-row WRITE rides a single endpoint and a failed post
+                    # releases what it began: nothing is running.
+                    cause = exc.__cause__ or exc
+                    if not isinstance(
+                        cause, (nixlNotFoundError, nixlRemoteDisconnectError)
+                    ):
+                        raise
+                    logger.warning(
+                        "Host staging WRITE not posted room=%s seq=%s: %r",
+                        part.room,
+                        part.seq,
+                        exc,
+                    )
+                    self._finish(slot, "ERR")
+            return
+        try:
+            state = self.xfer_state(slot.handle)
+        except nixlNotFoundError:
+            # A disconnect seen on another handle dropped this peer's metadata, so
+            # NIXL cannot read this WRITE until the transfer worker reloads it
+            # (conn.py fails a batch whose WRITE has a failed part, which runs
+            # that reload). It may still be writing: keep it under its deadline.
+            state = "PROC"
+        if state == "PROC":
+            if time.monotonic() - part.requested >= POST_DEADLINE_S + WRITE_DEADLINE_S:
+                fail_stop(f"Host staging WRITE timeout room={part.room} seq={part.seq}")

reviews.body:
Layering question before the line comments. What this PR does is transport work: pack strided descriptors into a contiguous pinned buffer, send one message, unpack on the far side. NIXL already receives the full descriptor list, so a staged-DRAM path inside the UCX backend (or a NIXL plugin) would keep sglang's contract unchanged: pages are owned by the sender until the transfer status is terminal. Every lifetime hook in this PR (`is_source_pending`, `holds_failed_source`, the extra collective, the guards in `mem_cache/common.py`, the PP rework) exists only because the gather reads source pages after `send()` returns on a stream outside the transfer worker. Has this been raised with the NIXL maintainers?   CC: @iyastreb @ovidiusm

Two things I think would be better to provide in the description regardless of where the code ends up:

1. Which deployments cannot get GPUDirect through either `nvidia-peermem` or DMA-BUF. That is the audience for the feature and it is not named.
2. A tuned baseline. The stock number (0.46 GiB/s) was taken with `UCX_IB_GPU_DIRECT_RDMA=n` and no UCX rendezvous tuning mentioned.

I would prefer everything needed to live entirely under `nixl/` behind the existing staging-handler interface, with the gather finished before `send()` returns. That costs some gather/WRITE overlap and tries hard to remove every change outside the NIXL directory (we are unifying the general logic: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/34510, backend-specific code in the prefill.py or decode.py will make it harder to refactor and maintain).
